ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Progress Note 7 — Focused Visit (Care-plan review) — Elvis Presley

code.originalText: Four-month review after the tour: recovery, the taper, blood pressure, weight, liver tests, sleep and the plan ahead

text.paragraph: Mr. Presley returns two weeks after finishing a three-week tour. He kept every weekly video visit on tour. He has taken buprenorphine 16 mg every morning with rare cravings and no other opioid, and diazepam 32 mg a day without withdrawal symptoms; he sleeps about seven hours with CPAP, on 88% of nights, and his Epworth score is 6. His home blood pressure averages 122/78. On tirzepatide 5 mg weekly for five weeks he has had mild nausea once and no constipation, and his weight is 102.6 kg. His bowels open daily or every other day on polyethylene glycol. He has no eye symptoms. He has started walking each morning and eating his main meal before the show. [S]

text.paragraph: Vital signs recorded on 2026-10-28; see the Vital Signs section. [S]

tr.td: Well; blood pressure 122/78, pulse 70; weight 102.6 kg, BMI 30.6

Fatigue, weight gain of about 14 kg in two years, constipation with a bowel movement every five to seven days, loud snoring with daytime sleepiness, and high blood pressure readings, in a man taking two opioids, two benzodiazepines and an appetite suppressant from five prescribers; under evaluation with addiction medicine, a sleep study and home blood pressure readings
S — Synthetic presenting problem anchored to the documented prescribed drugs and weight gain; superseded when the consultation and tests made the diagnoses.

Obesity, class 1 (BMI 32.5), with prediabetes (hemoglobin A1c 5.8%); recorded without stigma; weight gain began with long touring schedules, night eating after shows and an appetite suppressant that stopped working
S — Synthetic modern diagnosis anchored to his documented weight gain.

Glaucoma secondary to steroids, both eyes, mild stage, after an acute angle-closure episode treated years ago; intraocular pressure controlled on latanoprost under his ophthalmologist; anticholinergic and sympathomimetic drugs to be avoided
S — Synthetic modern diagnosis anchored to his documented glaucoma and the retrospective interpretation of it as steroid-induced; not a claim about his real eyes.

Opioid use disorder, severe, with prescription opioids from more than one prescriber (seven DSM-5-TR criteria, tolerance and withdrawal counted because the opioids were not taken as prescribed); on buprenorphine from the consultation; synthetic modern episode linked to his documented withdrawal from narcotic drugs and prescribed painkillers
S — Synthetic modern diagnosis made at the addiction medicine consultation; person-first language; not a claim about his real diagnosis.

Sedative, hypnotic, or anxiolytic use disorder (benzodiazepines), moderate (five DSM-5-TR criteria), with two benzodiazepines from two prescribers; combined into diazepam and tapering slowly; synthetic modern episode linked to his documented prescribed sedatives
S — Synthetic modern diagnosis made at the consultation; not a claim about his real diagnosis.
Hypertension, stage 2, confirmed by a home average of 146/94 a week after stopping phentermine; ECG and urine albumin normal
S — Synthetic modern diagnosis confirmed with home readings, anchored to his documented hypertension.
Obstructive sleep apnea, moderate (apnea-hypopnea index 26 an hour, central apnea index 4, oxygen nadir 80% on in-laboratory polysomnography), worsened by opioids and benzodiazepines; on CPAP
S — Synthetic modern diagnosis from a synthetic sleep study.
Opioid-induced constipation (Rome IV), improving after the change to buprenorphine; no alarm features
S — Synthetic modern diagnosis anchored to his documented blockage of the colon; not a claim about megacolon.
Acute low back strain after karate practice, without radicular signs or red flags, in a man on buprenorphine; resolved
S — Synthetic acute injury; not a historical claim.

list.item:
Opioid use disorder on buprenorphine (F11.20). In early remission on buprenorphine: no use of other opioids and rare cravings for more than three months. Safety reviewed: no thoughts of suicide or self-harm; naloxone on hand. [S]
Continue 16 mg daily without a planned end; visits every four weeks.
Counseling continues.

Benzodiazepine use disorder on a diazepam taper (F13.20). Five weeks at 32 mg without symptoms; the next step is due. [S]
Diazepam 30 mg a day (10 mg three times daily); the 2 mg tablets stopped.
Further steps of about 10% every four weeks, with CBT.

Hypertension, stage 2 (I10). At target on amlodipine with valsartan, helped by weight loss; potassium and creatinine normal. [S]
Continue; consider lowering the dose if weight loss continues and readings fall below 115/75.

Obesity, class 1, with prediabetes (E66.811). Down 5.9%, with hemoglobin A1c now 5.5% and liver tests normal. [S]
Continue tirzepatide 5 mg weekly; increase to 7.5 mg in four weeks if tolerated.

Obstructive sleep apnea on CPAP (G47.33). Good adherence and normal sleepiness score; weight loss may lower the pressure needed. [S]
Continue CPAP; repeat sleep testing if weight loss reaches 10%.

list.item: Stop full-agonist opioids and stabilize on buprenorphine without significant withdrawal. Outcome by 2026-08-07: Buprenorphine 16 mg a day since the consultation; no withdrawal after the first day; cravings low [S]
One prescriber and one pharmacy for all controlled medicines. Outcome by 2026-09-23: Monitoring program shows only this clinic's prescriptions since intake [S]

Lower the diazepam dose slowly, 5 to 10% every two to four weeks, toward stopping. Outcome by 2026-10-28: 40 mg a day after the alprazolam was combined into it, to 30 mg at four months; no withdrawal symptoms; taper continuing [S]
Home blood pressure below 130/80. Outcome by 2026-08-07: Home average 146/94 to 126/80 on amlodipine and valsartan [S]
Lose 5% or more of body weight. Outcome by 2026-10-28: 109.0 to 102.6 kg (5.9%) on tirzepatide, with more activity and earlier meals [S]
CPAP on at least 70% of nights for four hours or more, with less daytime sleepiness. Outcome by 2026-10-28: CPAP on 88% of nights; Epworth 14 to 6 [S]
A bowel movement at least every two days without straining. Outcome by 2026-08-07: Every one to two days on buprenorphine and polyethylene glycol [S]
